text: A number of studies have attempted to compare muscular adaptations between loading zones over time. Those investigating heavy versus medium loading have generally favored the hypertrophy range when volume was not equated between groups. Choi and colleagues (48) randomly assigned 1 1 young men to either a bulk-up protocol of 9 sets of knee extensions at 40% to 80% of 1RM with 30 seconds of rest between sets or a power-up protocol consisting of 5 sets at 90% of 1RM with 3 minutes of rest between sets. After 8 weeks, the results showed significantly greater increases in quadriceps hypertrophy for the bulk-up group.
